comparator.name: English Language and Culture
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA study-programme page accounts for the complete 180-EC English Language and Culture bachelor. Year 1 comprises ten compulsory 6-EC courses across English linguistics, literature, theory, rhetoric and writing, textual research and linguistic research methods. Year 2 contains three named compulsory literature/research courses (18 EC), 18 EC of restricted-choice core, 12 EC of programme-related electives and 12 EC of free choice. Year 3 contains Philosophy of the Humanities, Debates in English Studies, English Research Seminar, 30 EC of free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. The normalized target is generic and the official programme offers World Literatures in English or English Linguistics and Literature in years 2 and 3. English Linguistics and Literature most broadly preserves the programme title’s combined language-and-literature identity, so it is selected under the neutral broad-academic-identity rule before UCR course selection. The route is instantiated with the official linguistics-side restricted-choice core options, English Linguistics 5: Language in Society (12 EC) and English Linguistics 6: The Changing English Language (6 EC); genuine programme-related and free-choice space remains explicit rather than being filled with invented electives.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target names the general English Language and Culture bachelor rather than one specialisation. Of the two official specialisations, English Linguistics and Literature most broadly preserves the programme title’s combined language-and-literature identity, while World Literatures in English is the more specialised literature route. The combined route is selected independently of UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad closest match is complemented by two feasible generator-backed directions: world literatures with textual interpretation and cultural power, and English with identity and global culture. Each produces a materially different curriculum and exceeds the pairwise 30-EC/four-course distinctness floor, so the maximum of three alternatives is reached.

notes.text: The UvA programme provides a specialist sequence in English literary history, English linguistics and World Englishes, with route-specific core choice, a research seminar and a dedicated English Language and Culture thesis. UCR can build coherent literature/culture/language, literature/media and English/identity/global-culture pathways, but it does not reproduce the full English phonology, morphology, grammar, sociolinguistics and period-literature sequence or the dedicated English thesis structure.
